requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, the 'What are you importing?' page shows the same title, caption, heading, label, buttons, Cancel link and back link (to the origin page) as the live-animals page, including the inset 'You must submit a separate notification for every single health certificate. You must also submit a notification for goods that do not need an health certificate.'; its search hint reads 'You can search for semen, ova or embryos, or by common name (for example, cattle), Latin name (Bos taurus) or commodity code (05119985).', and continuing with nothing selected shows 'Select a commodity' in the error summary.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 tells a trader importing germinal products what they can search for, and changes nothing else on the page. The 9 October afternoon ruling lets the germinal set's copy of today's commodity page, with this hint, go ahead on today's commodity data; its errors are the live-animal page's, which the germinal specs show as 'Select a commodity'.
requirements.deltaNote: The real animals frontend has no germinal products set today.

requirements.statement: The germinal products set's commodity search offers only germinal-product commodities, so it never offers a live-animal commodity.
requirements.why: Each set holds one category, so a consignment mixing live animals and germinal products is never written, and the germinal set's own pages and search are not blocked on MDM. Taking today's germinal lines out of the live-animals catalogue is not this programme's work: ruling 10 November puts that in the separate commodity-search ticket's hands, which req-1754 records.
requirements.deltaNote: There is no germinal set today and its search does not exist; the 12 germinal lines it offers are the ones the live-animals commodity catalogue holds (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-026). Taking those lines out of the live-animals catalogue is the separate commodity-search ticket's work (req-1754).

requirements.statement: The germinal products catalogue holds the 12 specified germinal commodities, with embryos and ova as separate items: Cattle, Goat, Horse, Pig and Sheep each as '<Animal>, Embryos' and '<Animal>, Ova' (05119985); and '<Animal>, Semen' for Cattle (05111000), Cat, Dog, Goat, Horse, Pig, Rabbit/Rodent and Sheep (05119985): 18 items, sorted by name, codes shown with their leading zero. Each item offers the species listed under that animal (Cattle: Bison bison, Bos taurus and Bubalus bubalis, plus Bovidae for semen; Horse: Equus asinus and Equus caballus; Goat: Capra hircus; Pig: Sus scrofa domesticus; Sheep: Ovis aries; Cat: Felis catus; Dog: Canis familiaris; Rabbit/Rodent semen: one row labelled Rabbit/Rodent). There are no poultry, fish, bee, amphibian, arachnid or reptile germinal products and no Cat or Dog embryos or ova.
requirements.why: Out of scope: a commodity catalogue's names, codes, species, search terms and tariff codes are reference-list content, which is MDM's and reaches the service through trade-imports-reference-data, never edited in code and never a reason to block a row (ruling:ian-2026-11-11 points 2 and 3). The germinal catalogue's content therefore leaves the backlog as an MDM concern, exactly as the live-animals catalogue's content already has (req-094 to req-101), and c-282 records the clause that had blocked it. What the data page still decides is which germinal commodities the germinal fields apply to, naming the same twelve entries in all five of its applicability lists, and that is carried by req-121, req-123, req-124 and req-251. The 26 November prototype's Cat and Dog embryos and ova and its new Amphibian, Arachnid and Reptile embryos are mock data the 9 October ruling does not copy, and the data page gives them no fields (c-230). The page writes the codes without their leading zero and never says how they map to the codes a notification carries, which c-340 settles in favour of the eight-digit codes the catalogue and MDM use.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, each species block on Commodity details asks 'Total gross weight' in a narrow text input with the suffix 'kg', for every germinal commodity in the catalogue. It is optional: left blank, no error is shown, and the trader enters the figure.
requirements.why: The owner's 27 November ruling keeps the germinal total gross weight per species, as the 9 October ruling has each line's gross weight; V4 makes the total gross weight in kilograms an optional numeric field the trader supplies, with the example 24.50, and marks it as affecting the germinal journey only. V4's weight row is the one germinal row with no 'Applicable to' list, so it never says which germinal commodity codes the field is asked for; as the germinal set holds only germinal commodities and the other five germinal fields apply to all twelve entries, it is asked on every germinal species block. Design Release 2.1 gives the 'kg' suffix.

requirements.statement: The germinal set stores each species line's 'Total gross weight' answer as that line's gross weight in kilograms, held as a decimal, and shows it back in the service; it is not published on GBN-AG, because the current PIMS profile (gbn-ag-pims v0.2.0) has no gross weight.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks, errors and reviews the answer as a total gross weight, the owner keeps it per species, and what the real record stores is persistence, so no prototype storage key decides the quantity. The ruling publishes only what v0.2.0 already carries.
requirements.deltaNote: Today each commodity complement and species line records only whole-number animal and package counts, with no gross weight (repo-backend-p1-039, p1-040, p1-043, p1-044, cited in the backend's own area). The line's quantity stays its number of packages (c-234); only the gross weight is a decimal.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, each species block on Commodity details asks 'Number of packages', and the trader enters the count; germinal species are not asked the number of animals.
requirements.why: The owner's 27 November ruling keeps each chosen species' own number of packages, and the germinal set counts germinal products by package, not by head. V4 holds the germinal quantity on each commodity line and marks it as affecting the germinal journey only; its quantity row is the other germinal row with no 'Applicable to' list, so it never says which germinal commodity codes it is asked for, and as the set holds only germinal commodities it is asked on every species block.

requirements.statement: The germinal set's Commodity details page always asks one 'Temperature' radio question, once for the whole page, with the options Ambient, Chilled and Frozen in that order. It is optional: left unanswered, no error is shown. The answer is stored on every commodity line of the notification.
requirements.why: The option B plan always asks the temperature in the germinal set; V4 captures the temperature on each commodity line as an optional single-select the trader answers, with exactly those three values, the example Frozen, and the same twelve germinal commodities the other germinal fields apply to, and marks it as affecting the germinal journey only. The question's legend, hint and place on the page are Design Release 2.1's, weighed with the Commodity details page.

requirements.statement: A germinal-product commodity has one Selected commodities row listing all its chosen species (for example '05111000 | Cattle, Semen | Bos taurus'), its block is headed '<name> (<code>)' such as 'Cattle, Semen (05111000)', and its species sections are separated by section breaks.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lays germinal products out commodity by commodity, and the germinal pages are copies of their live-animals twins plus the prototype's germinal differences, which the 10 October ruling keeps in the germinal set's copies.

requirements.statement: A germinal products notification is started by the germinal set's own start (reached from the type question's Germinal products option or from 'Create new' on the germinal set's own notification list at /germinal-products), which creates the draft and skips the notification type question. It opens at the origin page, headed 'Origin of the import', which shows only 'Save and continue' and whose back link returns to the germinal set's own notification list, and then runs through 'What are you importing?' and 'Main import reason' to Commodity details as live animals does.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives germinal products their own entry point; the real services start each set from its own route rather than the prototype's create-notification?category= link. The prototype's germinal dashboard is the germinal set's own list, and the INS germinal list's 'Create new' leaves this programme with the INS home (c-281).

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, the page headed 'Main import reason' offers only Internal market and Transit, in that order, and ends with Save and continue, Save and return to overview and 'Cancel and return to overview'. Its other wording is the live-animals page's, apart from the two germinal hints.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 narrows the reasons for germinal products and words their hints for consignments rather than animals; the germinal page is otherwise a copy of its live-animals twin.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, Internal market reveals 'Purpose in the internal market' with only Transfer of ownership - Sale/gift, Breeding, Research and Production, in that order, each with its germinal hint; a submitted purpose outside these four counts as not chosen, and no purpose chosen shows 'Select a purpose in the internal market'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 narrows the internal market purposes for germinal products.

requirements.statement: The germinal products set has no Additional details page and no Additional details task: the hub's section 2 holds 'Commodity details', and 'Identification details' where it applies, only, and 'Save and continue' on a valid identification page reached through the journey goes straight to Arrival details; opened from its overview task, the review or the template review, the identification page returns there instead.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 hides the certification question for germinal products and no germinal commodity has unweaned options, so the page has nothing to ask; the ruling's option B plan leaves the page out of the set.

requirements.statement: A germinal product needs one set of identification details per species, whatever its quantity: its panel shows one editable form headed 'Enter details for <species>' (no count, such as 'Enter details for Bos taurus'), prefilled with what was saved, with no panel button and no saved-entries table. The page's own 'Save and continue' and 'Save and return to overview' both save the values typed into each germinal species' form.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 identifies germinal products once per species, not per package; the real store already holds one line per species. V4 holds the four germinal identifiers at unit level without saying how many unit records a germinal line carries, so the ruling and Design Release 2.1 set the count at one per species.

requirements.statement: Every germinal products commodity asks for 'Donor name/ID' (text), 'Collection date', 'Production date' and 'Identification number/mark' (text), in that order: four unit-level identifiers the trader enters, which apply to every germinal commodity in the catalogue.
requirements.why: The Live Animals & Germinals Data Fields V4 page sets the identifiers a germinal products notification captures, holds all four at unit level, has the trader supply every one of them, marks them as affecting the germinal journey only, and gives each the same twelve germinal commodity entries, so one applicability list covers all of them; Design Release 2.1 asks them in this order.

requirements.statement: Each germinal date field has a 'Choose date' calendar toggle, the Ministry of Justice date picker the live animals dates use, opening a month grid with previous and next year and month buttons, 'Select' and 'Close', over the single text input the field already has, so the field still works with the calendar unavailable.
requirements.why: The interaction designer's answer keeps the MOJ date picker on the germinal dates, and Sam's 10 November ruling takes the calendar out of the waiting-on-design theme and builds it with the germinal identification dates, germinal products following live animals rather than being a design question. It enhances the single text input req-2097 builds, because a page works fully without JavaScript and JavaScript only enhances one that already works (c-283).

requirements.statement: A Donor name/ID over 58 characters shows 'Donor name/ID must be 58 characters or less', in the error summary and inline; any characters are accepted up to that length.
requirements.why: V4 limits the donor name or ID to 58 characters and sets no character set, pattern or minimum length for it, its example GB1238765 being an example rather than a format; Design Release 2.1 gives the message.

requirements.statement: Germinal dates accept one- or two-digit day and month (such as 1/9/2026), any real date past or future, and a production date is not checked against the collection date; they read back as entered.
requirements.why: Neither V4 nor Design Release 2.1 sets a range or ordering rule on these dates; V4 only asks for a valid DD/MM/YYYY date, and its own example 12/12/2026 for both dates is in the future, so a future date is allowed.

requirements.statement: Each germinal identification field is optional on its own, so a partly or wholly blank entry saves without a missing-value error and never blocks 'Save and continue' (only the length and date rules apply to what is entered). But every selected germinal species, a lone species included, counts as identified only once its entry holds at least one of the four identifiers, and that one bar decides both submit and the hub's 'Identification details' Complete status. The identification page shows no message for this rule.
requirements.why: V4 marks all four germinal identifiers Optional and marks no germinal field mandatory to submit, while its own opening rule requires at least one germinal identifier per animal without naming which fields count or how 'per animal' maps to its unit records; the 9 October ruling settles that silence by making one identifier enough for both Complete and submit.

requirements.statement: A germinal product's identification panel keeps the species heading and the 'Change number of animals' link (to Commodity details), worded as for live animals.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 does not reword the panel for packages, the prototype decides wording, and the germinal pages take live animals as their reference for everything.

requirements.statement: Germinal products is its own set in trade-imports-animals-frontend, SET_ID 'germinal-products', mounted at /germinal-products beside live-animals, with its own journey, obligations, flow, cookies, gateway (routes-germinal-products.js) and set services. Its journey pages sit at /germinal-products/notifications/{journeyId}/{slug} using the live-animals slugs, each a copy of its live-animals feature folder plus the germinal differences; its overview, check answers, declaration and confirmation pages are its own copies too. Every live-animal field not marked as applying to the animal journey only is carried over; the CPH number and permanent address, which apply to the animal journey only, are not, so the set has no CPH number page and no permanent address page. The plants frontend has no germinal set, so no germinal-only difference changes plants.
requirements.why: Duplicating pages via features is the app's architecture and is desired, and option B of the germinal options paper was chosen over option A; the prototype's flat paths are not copied. V4's germinal section marks its seven fields as affecting the germinal journey only and names only the CPH number and permanent address as not required for germinal products, without saying which other live-animal fields the germinal journey drops or keeps and without a header row of its own, so the germinal field list is read from the ruling's copy rule plus V4's own per-field markings rather than from the germinal table alone (req-1832, req-1833). The copy of each live-animals page is taken after this programme has built the live twin. The 9 October afternoon ruling leaves plants unchanged by rows it has no equivalent of and never mirrors animals-only data into it.

requirements.statement: A germinal products notification is created with Draft status and the same kind of reference as a live-animals one, GBN-AG followed by the two-digit year and six characters; from the first page the status strip reads 'Draft' then 'Germinal products - ' and the reference. No GBN-GP reference is ever issued.
requirements.why: Germinal notifications keep GBN-AG references; GBN-GP references are demonstration data only. Design Release 2.1 names the category in the status strip.
requirements.deltaNote: Today only live-animals notifications exist; each is minted a GBN-AG-YY-XXXXXX reference at creation (repo-frontend-p2-009, trace-e2e-p13-004, repo-tests-p2-115).

requirements.statement: Searching 'semen' in the germinal set lists the eight semen commodities in name order (Cat, Semen; Cattle, Semen (05111000); Dog, Semen; Goat, Semen; Horse, Semen; Pig, Semen; Rabbit/Rodent, Semen; Sheep, Semen, all others 05119985), offering 12 species rows, and the live region announces '12 results available'; searching 'embryo' lists the embryos and ova commodities.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the commodity search is handled by a separate ticket rather than by this work, and a search listing germinal codes belongs to that ticket (ruling:sam-2026-11-10, c-382). EUDPA-616 owns the commodity type-ahead and EUDPA-569 'Germinal | Commodity search' the germinal catalogue it searches. What the search would list is a commodity catalogue's content, which is MDM's and is never edited in code (c-282, req-093).

requirements.statement: Ticking a germinal species, such as Domestic cattle (Bos taurus) under Cattle, Semen, shows '1 selected' with a 'Cattle, Semen (05111000):' line and a remove button named 'Remove Domestic cattle (Bos taurus)', as the live-animal search does.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows germinal selections the same way as live-animal ones, and the germinal commodity page is a copy of its live-animals twin, so its selected panel is the live page's panel over the germinal lines the catalogue holds.

requirements.statement: A Total gross weight that is not a number greater than 0 (digits with an optional decimal part; no sign, commas or units), such as 0 or 'abc', shows 'Enter a number greater than 0', linked from the 'There is a problem' error summary to that species' field and shown inline with the 'Error:' prefix, with what was entered kept; spaces around the figure are ignored.
requirements.why: V4 and Design Release 2.1 both require the weight to be above 0; Design Release 2.1 gives the message, trims the figure and re-shows what was entered.

requirements.statement: A Total gross weight over 1,000 shows 'Total gross weight must be 1,000kg or less', linked to that species' field and shown inline; 1,000 itself is accepted.
requirements.why: V4 caps the total gross weight at 1,000 kg. Its conditions cell is empty and Design Release 2.1 shows no maximum, so neither gives the message or says what happens at exactly 1,000; the message and the inclusive limit follow the GOV.UK pattern for a maximum.

requirements.statement: A Total gross weight accepts up to 2 decimal places (12.5 and 24.50 are accepted); more shows 'Total gross weight must have 2 decimal places or fewer', linked to that species' field and shown inline.
requirements.why: V4 gives the weight to 2 decimal places, with 24.50 as its example, and the ruling holds it as a decimal; Design Release 2.1 accepts 12.5. V4 states no rounding rule, so a figure with more decimal places is refused with a message rather than rounded, following the GOV.UK pattern.

requirements.statement: Number of packages is required: left blank, it shows 'Enter the number of packages', linked from the error summary to that species' field and shown inline.
requirements.why: V4 makes the line's quantity mandatory to proceed, the only mandatory field in its germinal section, and the line's quantity is its number of packages (c-234).

requirements.statement: A Number of packages that is not a whole number of 1 or more, such as 'x', shows 'Enter a whole number greater than 0', in the error summary and inline.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 counts packages in whole numbers from 1; V4 gives the quantity a maximum but no minimum, no decimal-place rule and an empty conditions cell, so it sets no minimum of its own and the prototype decides.

requirements.statement: A Number of packages over 1,000 shows 'Number of packages must be 1,000 or less', linked to that species' field and shown inline; 1,000 itself is accepted.
requirements.why: V4 caps the germinal quantity at 1,000, with 10 as its example. Neither V4 nor Design Release 2.1 gives the message, so it follows the GOV.UK pattern for a maximum.

requirements.statement: Valid germinal commodity details continue to Identification details, the page titled 'Identification details - Import notification service - GOV.UK' and headed 'Identification details'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's germinal journey reaches Identification details once the commodity answers are valid; with the gross weight asked on each species block, Commodity details leads straight there.

requirements.statement: An invalid germinal identification submission re-renders the page with the error summary titled 'There is a problem'; its errors are listed in field order (Donor name/ID, Collection date, Production date, Identification number/mark), each linking to its own field, which is shown in error with the message inline after the 'Error:' prefix.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows germinal errors in the standard GOV.UK way, and V4's four identifiers are asked in this order.

requirements.statement: A submitted main reason outside the germinal set's two (such as Re-entry) is saved as no reason.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 accepts only the reasons offered to the notification, and the germinal set offers only Internal market and Transit.

requirements.statement: Each germinal products trade line in the published GBN-AG payload carries the typeCode for its product type: SEMEN for a semen line, EMBRYO for an embryos line and OVA for an ova line. A commodity that is embryos and a commodity that is ova are separate commodities, each its own trade line, never one 'Embryos/Ova' line.
requirements.why: The GBN-AG schema names these codes, and the 9 October ruling makes the schema, not the prototype's mock data, decide them. The rule is written by product type, so a separate ova commodity takes OVA as soon as the catalogue holds one; a combined 'Embryos/Ova' line, while the catalogue holds one, takes EMBRYO (req-1928). A catalogue's content is MDM's and is never a reason to block a row (c-282). Live-animal lines carry LIVE_ANIMAL (req-1894).
requirements.deltaNote: Today trade lines carry no typeCode (repo-backend-p6-109, c-273). Until this lands, today's lines carry the interim codes of req-1928.

requirements.statement: Publishing to PIMS the germinal products details it has no field for (temperature, donor name/ID, collection and production dates, identification mark, decimal kilogram quantity, each line's gross weight) through a new GBN-AG profile version.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the PIMS schema update is EUDPA-686, a Jira ticket outside the backlog that starts after this programme lands, and its shape is not yet known.

requirements.statement: Capturing an approved establishment on a germinal products notification.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the data fields page's change log records the germinal Approved Establishment field as de-scoped on 7 September 2026, with no reason given and no field row left on the page, which outranks any source that still describes it.

requirements.statement: Capturing a package type on a germinal products notification.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the data fields page's change log records the germinal Package type field as de-scoped on 7 September 2026, and Design Release 2.1's germinal commodities carry no packaging fields. An unresolved inline comment hangs on the change-log row and its text is not in the fetched page, so whatever it questions is not recorded.

requirements.statement: A k6 performance journey for the germinal products set.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the performance suite has no germinal set base, steps or endpoints, and its catalogue names no germinal route, so nothing the germinal set adds breaks one of its k6 scripts; the suite changes only where a row breaks a script it already has (c-225). The ruling places the germinal set's specs in the animals Playwright project and names no performance work.

requirements.statement: The germinal set's end-to-end, accessibility and security specs live in the tests repo's existing animals Playwright project, under tests/animals/e2e/germinal-products, tests/animals/a11y/germinal-products and tests/animals/security/germinal-products; no new Playwright project is made, and INS-side germinal work is proven in the ins project. The accessibility specs walk the germinal journey and hold each page to WCAG 2.2 AA on initial load and with answers filled, under the suite's existing axe rules, and the security specs drive the germinal routes through the ZAP scan.
requirements.why: The germinal set is still the animals frontend, and the ruling places its specs there.
requirements.deltaNote: The accessibility and security suites today cover only the live-animals journey (repo-tests-p6-021, p6-042, p6-091, cited in the tests repo's own area).

requirements.statement: The germinal products set's 'What are you importing?' page, with its germinal search hint, offers the 12 germinal lines the commodity catalogue holds, with their existing names and codes and with embryos and ova as one combined 'Embryos/Ova' line, found through a server-side search behind the Search button, with no results shown as the trader types.
requirements.why: The 9 October afternoon ruling splits the germinal commodity work so the germinal set is not held up by the catalogue: the page's wording (req-069) and place in the journey go ahead on the commodity data the service has, and that search already works without JavaScript. The catalogue's own content is MDM's (c-282).
requirements.deltaNote: There is no germinal set today; the 12 germinal lines sit in the live-animals catalogue (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-026) and the germinal set's search offers them (req-092). Taking them out of the live-animals catalogue is the separate commodity-search ticket's work (req-1754, c-222).

requirements.statement: A combined 'Embryos/Ova' germinal trade line in the published GBN-AG payload carries the typeCode EMBRYO, and a semen line carries SEMEN, so a combined line records its ova as embryos.
requirements.why: The GBN-AG schema has no combined embryos-and-ova code, and the commodity catalogue still holds combined lines; the 9 October afternoon ruling sets EMBRYO as the default, which Sam has not objected to.
requirements.deltaNote: Today trade lines carry no typeCode (repo-backend-p6-109, c-273).

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set's identification page, Collection date and Production date are each a single text input with the hint 'For example, 27/03/2026', which works without JavaScript.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives both dates this hint, and the 9 October afternoon ruling builds them now as single text inputs. Same change as req-252 (another area's); the cross-area pass merges them.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, an Identification number/mark over 58 characters shows 'Identification number/mark must be 58 characters or less', in the error summary and inline; any characters are accepted up to that length.
requirements.why: V4 limits the identification number or mark to 58 characters and sets no character set, pattern or minimum length, its example GB1238765 being an example rather than a format; Design Release 2.1 gives the message in the Donor name/ID pattern. Same change as req-255 (another area's); the cross-area pass merges them.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, a Collection date not in the form day/month/four-digit year shows 'Enter a collection date in the format DD/MM/YYYY', in the error summary and inline.
requirements.why: V4 requires a valid DD/MM/YYYY collection date; the message follows Design Release 2.1's production date message. Same change as req-256 (another area's); the cross-area pass merges them.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, a Production date not in the form day/month/four-digit year, such as 2026-09-01, shows 'Enter a production date in the format DD/MM/YYYY', in the error summary and inline.
requirements.why: V4 requires a valid DD/MM/YYYY production date and Design Release 2.1 gives the message. Same change as req-257 (another area's); the cross-area pass merges them.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, a Collection date in the right format that is not a real date, such as 99/99/2026, shows 'Collection date must be a real date', in the error summary and inline.
requirements.why: V4 requires a valid collection date and Design Release 2.1 gives the message. Same change as req-258 (another area's); the cross-area pass merges them.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, a Production date in the right format that is not a real date shows 'Production date must be a real date', in the error summary and inline.
requirements.why: V4 requires a valid production date; the message follows Design Release 2.1's collection date message. Same change as req-259 (another area's); the cross-area pass merges them.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, the identification page's 'Selected commodities' quantity column is headed 'Number of packages' and shows each species' saved count, where live animals show Number of animals.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 counts germinal products by package on the identification page too, and the owner keeps each species' own number of packages. Same change as req-1776 (another area's); the cross-area pass merges them.

requirements.statement: The germinal products set's origin page asks for and records the same four origin answers as the live-animals set: the country of origin, whether a region of origin code is required, the region of origin code and the internal reference number.
requirements.why: Each germinal page is a copy of its live-animals feature folder plus the prototype's germinal differences, Design Release 2.1 uses the same 'Origin of the import' page for germinal products, and the data page's germinal section names only the county parish holding number and the permanent address as not required for germinal products, saying nothing about the origin page's fields, so the germinal origin page asks what the live-animals origin page asks.
requirements.deltaNote: No germinal products set exists in the animals frontend today.

requirements.statement: In the germinal-products set, choosing Transit on the main import reason reveals the same two selects as the live-animals set, in the same order, 'Port of exit' then 'Destination country': the same lists, the same 'Select one' placeholder, the same labels with no hint, and the same 'Select a port of exit' and 'Select a destination country' messages, in that order, when either is missing.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's germinal reason page offers Transit, and its Transit reveal holds the same exit port and destination country selects as live animals with the same messages. The prototype decides which questions are asked of which goods, and each germinal page is a copy of its live-animals twin plus the prototype's germinal differences, so a germinal Transit notification captures both.
requirements.deltaNote: No germinal-products set exists in the real frontend today.

requirements.statement: The germinal products set has no exit date question, and no germinal page asks when the consignment leaves Great Britain.
requirements.why: The owner's 27 November ruling keeps the default: the germinal products set offers only Internal market and Transit, asks for no exit date and builds nothing for one, while the live-animals set keeps its own exit date question (c-331).
requirements.deltaNote: No germinal-products set exists in the real frontend today.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, the identification page asks for none of the live-animal identifiers: it asks only for the germinal fields, donor name or ID, collection date, production date and identification number or mark.
requirements.why: The data page's germinal section defines the data elements that apply to germinal products only, every one of its fields impacts the germinal journey alone, and the county parish holding number and permanent address apply to the animal journey only; Design Release 2.1's germinal commodities carry no animal identifiers, so the germinal set's copy of the page carries only the four germinal fields.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, 'Save and return to overview' makes exactly the same checks as 'Save and continue' on every page that shows both buttons, the set's own Commodity details and Identification details pages included: a missing or invalid answer keeps the trader on the page with an error in the summary and inline for each one and what they entered kept, and with nothing missing or invalid the answers are saved and the overview is shown.
requirements.why: The two save buttons behaving alike, with no page an exception, is what the owner decided, and the 27 November ruling names the germinal products copy among the pages it reaches; a trader who saves and returns otherwise leaves a page holding answers the service has not checked, and the germinal-only weight, package, length and date rules would be made by one button and not the other. How far the checks reach on a page is settled elsewhere (c-372).

requirements.statement: The germinal-products set asks the same arrival questions as the live-animals set: its arrival details page asks the same five questions in the same wording and order with the same rules, and its transit countries page asks the same question, appearing only when the means of transport is rail or road.
requirements.why: Each germinal page is a copy of its live-animals feature folder plus the prototype's germinal differences, the data page's germinal section names only the county parish holding number and the permanent address as not required for germinal products and says nothing about the arrival, transport or transited-countries fields, and the prototype decides which questions are asked of which goods. Design Release 2.1's germinal journey moves goods through Great Britain under Transit, which c-344 settles.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, a new draft records 'Germinal products' as what the consignment is certified for, without asking the trader and with no way to change it.
requirements.why: Germinal products is a set of its own, so what the consignment is certified for follows from the set the trader started in rather than from a question; the option B plan the owner chose sets the answer when the draft is created and shows it with no Change link, which is why the set asks no certification question (req-181). Design Release 2.1 carries a certification purpose list (Breeding and/or production, Approved bodies, Other) on every germinal commodity that no germinal page reads.

requirements.statement: A separate 'What is the total gross weight of the consignment?' page after Commodity details, asking one required total gross weight for the whole consignment, with the caption 'Description of the goods', the hint 'This includes the weight of all the commodities in the consignment and their packaging.', its own back links, completeness rule and form actions.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the owner's 27 November ruling, given after the prototype moved to this page, keeps the germinal total gross weight per species on Commodity details (req-121, c-231), and V4 makes the weight optional (c-232). The page's mechanisms (pre-filling from earlier per-species net weights, minting a prototype reference on visit, saving without checks on Save and return) exist for the prototype's own session data. What still holds from the page is carried per species: the number rule and trimming (req-1784), decimals (req-1786) and continuing to Identification details (req-1790). Live animals have no total gross weight in either reading.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, the Internal market reason's hint reads 'For consignments intended for sale or use in Great Britain (England, Scotland or Wales).'
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 words the germinal reason hints for consignments, since germinal products are not animals; the prototype decides wording.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, the Transit reason's hint reads 'For consignments moving through Great Britain for direct travel to a third country, that will enter Great Britain at one port or airport and leave from a different one within England, Scotland or Wales.'
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 words the germinal reason hints for consignments; the prototype decides wording.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, the internal market purpose 'Transfer of ownership - Sale/gift' has the hint 'Any movement of a consignment that has as its aim the sale of or the transfer of ownership of the consignment from one person or entity to another.'
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives each germinal purpose its own hint; the prototype decides wording.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, the internal market purpose 'Breeding' has the hint 'Consignments for reproduction. This includes animals and germinal products intended to contribute to the genetic pool of a breeding program, improve livestock quality, or produce offspring.'
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives each germinal purpose its own hint; the prototype decides wording.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, the internal market purpose 'Research' has the hint 'Animals and germinal products for use in scientific or medical research.'
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives each germinal purpose its own hint; the prototype decides wording.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, the internal market purpose 'Production' has the hint 'Animals and germinal products that are farmed for the production of meat, milk, eggs, wool or any other animal product or by-product.'
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives each germinal purpose its own hint; the prototype decides wording.

conflicts.about: Whether the germinal weight is a gross or a net weight: V4 and the rulings say gross, while the prototype still falls back to per-species net weights an earlier version saved.

positions.says: A germinal products notification captures a 'Total gross weight (kg)' field.
In the germinal set, weight is a total gross weight in kilograms, held as a decimal.
The gross weight is pre-filled from the first saved per-species net weight when no gross weight is saved.

conflicts.outcome: Gross weight: the answer is stored as each line's gross weight in kilograms, as a decimal (ruling 9 October, V4), and shown but not published, because gbn-ag-pims v0.2.0 has no gross weight. The 26 November prototype itself now holds the answer as a gross weight; its fallback to per-species net weights saved by earlier versions is the prototype's own session mechanism and data-model shape is never the prototype's to decide, so only that fallback is set aside.

conflicts.about: How a germinal notification is routed: the prototype's flat pages and create-notification?category=germinal-products, or a sibling set of its own.

positions.says: /create-notification?category=germinal-products starts a germinal notification on the shared flat origin page, skipping the type question.
Germinal products is its own set at /germinal-products; the prototype's flat paths and ?category= routing are not copied.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: germinal products is a sibling set at /germinal-products with the live-animals slugs, started from its own route. The prototype's behaviour (skipping the type question, landing on origin, back to the germinal list) is kept; only its URL and query shape are not copied, so the specs claim still backs req-127 and is not overruled.

conflicts.about: Whether germinal-only behaviour depends on every chosen species being germinal, with mixed live-and-germinal consignments treated differently.

positions.says: The gross weight page is shown only when every selected species is a germinal product; otherwise it redirects onward.
Each set holds one category, so a mixed consignment is never written.
Every mixed-load criterion is dropped (req-124, req-169, req-170, req-181).

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: the germinal set holds only germinal products, so its weight, temperature question, two reasons and four purposes always apply, and there is no mixed case or later switch to germinal-only. The prototype's germinal-only conditions are set aside; the other mixed-load conditions are weighed with the commodity details and reason pages.

conflicts.about: Whether embryos and ova are one 'Embryos/Ova' catalogue item or two.

positions.says: Every germinal commodity is named '<Animal>, Embryos/Ova' or '<Animal>, Semen', 18 in all.
V4 lists 'Embryos/Ova - Cattle' as one entry under 5119985, among its twelve germinal entries.
Embryos and ova are separate items in the germinal catalogue; the prototype's single Embryos/Ova item is mock data and is not copied.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: embryos and ova are separate catalogue items, each with its own GBN-AG typeCode (EMBRYO, OVA), named '<Animal>, Embryos' and '<Animal>, Ova'. The prototype's Embryos/Ova naming is set aside. V4's entry still backs which animals have embryos and ova, so it is not overruled. While the catalogue holds a combined line, that line carries EMBRYO (req-1928), and a separate ova commodity takes OVA as soon as the catalogue holds one (req-1800); the catalogue's own content is MDM's (c-282).

conflicts.about: Which germinal commodities the catalogue holds: V4's 12 'Applicable to' entries, or Design Release 2.1's, which add Cat and Dog embryos/ova and, since 26 November, Amphibian, Arachnid and Reptile embryos/ova.

positions.says: The twelve Applicable to entries are embryos/ova of Cattle, Goat, Horse, Pig and Sheep and semen of Cattle, Dog or Cat, Goat, Horse, Pig, Rodent/Rabbit and Sheep.
Cat, Embryos/Ova (05119985, Felis catus) is a germinal commodity.
Dog, Embryos/Ova (05119985, Canis familiaris) is a germinal commodity.
Amphibian, Embryos/Ova (05119985) is a germinal commodity.
Arachnid, Embryos/Ova (05119985) is a germinal commodity.
Reptile, Embryos/Ova (05119985) is a germinal commodity.
The prototype's single 'Embryos/Ova' items are mock data and are not copied.
A reference list is MDM's content and never rests on the prototype's demo fixtures.

conflicts.outcome: The germinal fields apply to V4's 12 germinal commodities only, with embryos and ova split (ruling 9 October) and V4's 'Semen - Dog or Cat' shown as separate Cat, Semen and Dog, Semen. Cat and Dog embryos and ova, and the 26 November prototype's Amphibian, Arachnid and Reptile embryos, come only from the prototype's demo fixtures, which the 11 November ruling bars as evidence of which commodities exist, and V4 gives them no fields. Every V4 germinal field (temperature and the four Unit Level identifiers) therefore applies to every germinal commodity, all five of V4's applicability lists naming the same twelve entries, which req-121, req-123, req-124 and req-251 carry; the catalogue's content itself is MDM's and leaves the backlog (c-282, req-093), and the germinal set goes ahead on the germinal lines the catalogue holds (req-1927).

conflicts.about: Whether the germinal total gross weight is asked once for the whole consignment (V4, and the 26 November prototype's own page) or once per species line (the owner's rulings).

positions.says: Total gross weight (kg) applies at Notification level, the only germinal row that does.
The germinal section uses three levels: notification level for the total gross weight, commodity level for the quantity and temperature, and unit level for the four identifiers.
The gross weight page asks for one value for the whole consignment.
Total gross weight is one text input for the whole consignment.
The total gross weight is one field for the whole consignment.
Each germinal line has its own gross weight, stored but not published.
In the germinal products set, the number of packages and the total gross weight stay per species.

conflicts.outcome: The owner's 27 November ruling ranks first of all and was given after the prototype moved the weight to a page of its own: the germinal total gross weight stays per species, asked in each species block on Commodity details and stored as each line's gross weight, as the 9 October ruling also has it (req-121, req-122). V4's notification-level placement and the prototype's single consignment-level field are set aside, and with them the separate gross weight page (req-germinal-products-001). V4's three-level claim is not overruled: its commodity-level and unit-level placements still stand and back req-123, req-124 and req-251.

conflicts.about: Whether the germinal Total gross weight and Temperature are required (Design Release 2.1) or optional (V4).

positions.says: Total gross weight (kg) is optional.
Temperature is optional.
Quantity (unit/pieces) is the only mandatory field in the germinal section.
Total gross weight is required: blank shows 'Enter the total gross weight'.
For a germinal consignment the gross weight is complete only when it holds a number greater than 0.
A blank weight shows 'Enter the total gross weight'.
Continuing with no total gross weight shows 'Enter the total gross weight'.

conflicts.outcome: V4 ranks above the prototype and is the policy for whether a germinal field is mandatory; mandatory status is validation, which the prototype does not decide. Total gross weight and Temperature are optional, with no blank errors, and neither holds back the Commodity details task's Complete status (req-1763) nor appears in the error summary's order (req-1762). Number of packages stays required (V4: mandatory to proceed, and the only mandatory field in its germinal section), so its blank error stands (req-1787). The prototype's required weight and its completeness bar on the weight are set aside; its required temperature is weighed with the Commodity details page, where the same reasoning sets it aside for the germinal set.

conflicts.about: Whether the germinal temperature is one answer per page or one per commodity line (V4).

positions.says: Temperature applies at Commodity Level, so each commodity line carries one.
The germinal set always asks for temperature, as the option B plan sets out.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first and has the set always ask the temperature, which Design Release 2.1 asks once for the whole page; V4 decides data: every commodity line carries a temperature. Both are kept: the one answer is stored on every line (req-124). Neither claim is set aside.

conflicts.about: What a germinal line's quantity is: its number of packages, or its weight in kilograms.

positions.says: A germinal notification captures a 'Quantity (unit/pieces)' field, held on each commodity line.
The germinal 'decimal kilogram quantity' is stored but not published, because v0.2.0's quantity is a whole number.
The germinal weight is a total gross weight in kilograms held as a decimal.
Each chosen species under a commodity keeps its own number of packages.

conflicts.outcome: A germinal line's quantity is its number of packages, kept per species (ruling 27 November): the page asks 'Number of packages' and it takes V4's Quantity (unit/pieces) rules (required to proceed, a whole number from 1, at most 1,000). Being a whole number already carried by gbn-ag-pims v0.2.0, it fills that profile's quantity on GBN-AG. 'Total gross weight' is the line's gross weight in kilograms, stored as a decimal and shown in the service but not published, which is what the 9 October ruling means by the decimal kilogram quantity. The 26 November prototype's Commodity details block, which now asks a required 'Quantity (unit/pieces)' and an optional 'Number of packages' side by side, is weighed in the commodity details area; the cross-area pass reconciles it with this outcome.

conflicts.about: When a germinal species counts as identified: once its entry is saved even if blank (Design Release 2.1), or once it holds at least one identifier (V4 and the ruling).

positions.says: A germinal notification must be submitted with at least one germinal identifier per animal.
One identifier is enough: a record with one identifier counts as identified, for Complete and for submit.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling and V4 rank above the prototype: a germinal species counts as identified, for Complete and for submit, once its one entry holds at least one of the four identifiers. Each field stays optional on its own, so a blank entry still saves, but it does not count. The prototype's empty-entry rule is weighed in the identification area, where it is set aside for the germinal set by this outcome.

conflicts.about: Whether a germinal products notification with only one species selected may be submitted, and show its Identification details task Complete, with no identification details.

positions.says: A germinal products notification must be submitted with at least one germinal identifier per animal.
The section never says which of its fields count as a germinal identifier, nor how 'per animal' maps to the unit records the fields are captured at.
No row of the germinal table carries the submit-time rule: the quantity is the only mandatory field and the other six, the four identifiers included, are Optional.
One identifier is enough: a record with one identifier counts as identified, for the Complete status and for submit.

conflicts.outcome: V4 ranks above the prototype and is the policy for which germinal data is mandatory, and the 9 October ruling, ranking above V4, settles V4's own silence: V4 states the submit-time rule in its opening paragraph but carries it on no row and marks all four identifiers Optional, so the ruling sets the bar at one identifier and exempts no species. Every selected germinal species, a lone one included, needs its entry to hold at least one of the four identifiers before submit, and the Identification details task shows Complete on that same bar (req-261); the germinal review names any species short of it, however many are selected (req-1841). Under either reading of V4's 'per animal' (per species line or per notification) a single-species notification needs an identifier, so no question is left. The prototype's lone-species exemption is weighed in the identification and review areas, where it still sets the live-animals rule; it is not copied into the germinal set.

conflicts.about: Whether the INS germinal products list's 'Create new' starts the germinal set in this programme.

positions.says: The INS germinal list's 'Create new' starts the germinal set.
The INS germinal list's 'Create new' and the INS home's germinal section leave this programme with the INS home.
The germinal set's own copy of the reframed list sits at the set root, and its 'Create new' starts a germinal notification.
The type question's Germinal option stays the way into a germinal notification.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October afternoon ruling ranks first and withdraws the earlier claim: a germinal notification is started from the type question's Germinal products option or from 'Create new' on the germinal set's own list at /germinal-products, and the origin page's back link returns to that list. The INS germinal list's 'Create new' is not built in this programme.

conflicts.about: Whether the germinal products catalogue's own content, V4's 18 items with embryos and ova separate, is built in this programme, blocked on MDM, or left to MDM altogether.

positions.says: The germinal data applies to twelve named germinal commodities, embryos/ova of five species and semen of seven species groups.
Embryos and ova are separate items in the germinal catalogue.
V4's 18-item germinal catalogue waits on MDM.
Embryos and ova as separate items applies only once the catalogue is re-distilled; until then combined lines carry EMBRYO.
A reference list is MDM's content reaching the service through trade-imports-reference-data; it is never a reason to block a row and is never edited in code.

conflicts.outcome: The 11 November ruling ranks above the 9 October afternoon ruling: a commodity catalogue's names, codes and species are a reference list, so they are MDM's content, never edited in code and never a reason to block a row. The germinal catalogue's content therefore leaves the backlog as an MDM concern, as the live-animals catalogue's content already has, so req-093 and req-1782 are out of scope and the clause that blocked them on MDM is set aside. What V4 still decides is which germinal commodities the germinal fields apply to, which req-121, req-123, req-124 and req-251 carry. The germinal set goes ahead on the germinal lines the catalogue holds (req-1927), whose combined 'Embryos/Ova' lines carry EMBRYO and semen lines SEMEN (req-1928), and the typeCode rule is written by product type (req-1800), so a separate ova commodity takes OVA as soon as the catalogue holds one. The afternoon ruling's separate-items clause is not overruled: it still backs the split itself.

conflicts.about: Whether the germinal collection and production dates get the Ministry of Justice date picker's 'Choose date' calendar, and whether it waits on design.

positions.says: The germinal dates are built now as single text inputs, and the 'Choose date' calendar waits on design question 12, because MoJ advises against its date picker for dates read from a document.
The germinal date calendars keep the MOJ date picker.
The germinal date calendar work is merged into the germinal identification dates row.

conflicts.outcome: The interaction designer's 9 November answer and Sam's 10 November ruling both rank above the 9 October afternoon ruling: design has answered design question 12 and keeps the MOJ date picker on the germinal dates, and the calendar leaves the waiting-on-design theme to be built with the germinal identification dates, germinal products following live animals rather than being a design question. Each germinal date is a single text input with the hint 'For example, 27/03/2026' and V4's checks (req-2097), and the calendar sits over that input rather than replacing it, because a page works fully without JavaScript and JavaScript only enhances one that already works; that also answers what the 10 November ruling leaves unsaid about the input, its hint and its checks. Nothing is overruled: the afternoon ruling's single text input is what the picker enhances.

conflicts.about: Whether the germinal products set captures an exit date, which the copy rule would carry across from live animals while the only reasons the set offers never ask for one.

positions.says: The germinal reason page offers only Internal market and Transit, neither of which asks for an exit date.
Each germinal page is a copy of its live-animals feature folder plus the prototype's germinal differences, which carries the live-animals exit date page across.

The germinal section names only the county parish holding number and the permanent address as not required for germinal products, and does not say which other live-animal fields the germinal journey drops or keeps.
The germinal products set asks for no exit date, and nothing is built for one; the live-animals set keeps its own.

conflicts.outcome: The owner's 27 November ruling ranks first and keeps the default: the germinal products set offers only Internal market and Transit, asks for no exit date and builds nothing for one, and the live-animals set keeps its own exit date question (req-2141). Nothing is overruled: the copy rule still carries every other live-animals page across, and the data page's silence still stands as recorded.

conflicts.about: Whether the same-checks rule for Save and return to overview reaches the germinal products set, which the 26 October ruling does not name and whose prototype gross weight page saves without checks.

positions.says: The same-checks rule applies on every page that has both buttons, in the live animals frontend and in the high-risk plants frontend.
The ruling says nothing about the germinal-products set or any other frontend with both save buttons, so whether the rule reaches them is left open.
Each germinal page is a copy of its live-animals feature folder, taken after the live twin is built, plus the germinal differences.
No page is an exception to the same-checks rule.
The same save-button checks apply in live animals, in the germinal products copy and on plants' pages.
'Save and return to overview' on the gross weight page saves whatever was entered without validating it.

conflicts.outcome: The owner's 27 November ruling ranks first and names the germinal products copy, which closes the gap the 26 October ruling's wording left; that ruling's 'No page is an exception' already pointed the same way, and the 9 October copy rule carries the behaviour into every copied page. On every germinal page that shows both buttons the two make exactly the same checks, the set's own Commodity details and Identification details pages included, so the germinal weight, package, length and date rules are made on each (req-2162). The prototype's unchecked Save and return is set aside. The scope and gap claims still record what the 26 October ruling names and leaves unsaid, and the copy rule still stands. The same settlement is recorded page by page where each area met it, on the origin page (c-321), the commodity pages (c-323), the identification page and the contact address page (c-362); how far the checks reach on any one page is c-372.

conflicts.about: Whether a germinal commodity's code is the seven-digit number V4 writes or the eight-digit code the real catalogue and MDM carry.

positions.says: The twelve germinal entries are written as 5111000 and 5119985, with their leading zero dropped, and the page never says how they map to the codes a notification carries.
Cattle semen is 05111000, the only germinal commodity not under 05119985.
V4's 18-item germinal catalogue waits on MDM.
The rest of the commodities area goes ahead on today's commodity data.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October afternoon ruling ranks first: a germinal commodity's code is whatever the catalogue carries, today's commodity data now and MDM's once commodities come from it, which is the eight-digit 05111000 for cattle semen and 05119985 for every other germinal commodity, shown with its leading zero as Design Release 2.1 shows it. V4's seven-digit 5111000 and 5119985 are the same codes with the leading zero dropped, and no code is edited in the service to match the page. Nothing is overruled: V4's entries still back which germinal commodities the data applies to, and its gap claim still records that the page states no mapping, which is why the catalogue rather than the page decides the code.

conflicts.about: Whether the germinal products set asks for transit countries, which Design Release 2.1's germinal journey reaches under Transit while the data page leaves the set's other live-animal fields unsaid.

positions.says: The germinal section names only the county parish holding number and the permanent address as not required for germinal products and does not say which other live-animal fields the germinal journey drops or keeps.
The germinal Transit reason is for consignments moving through Great Britain to a third country, entering at one port or airport and leaving from a different one.
The prototype decides which questions are asked of which goods.
Each germinal page is a copy of its live-animals feature folder plus the prototype's germinal differences.

conflicts.outcome: Sam's 9 October ruling ranks above the data page and gives the prototype which questions are asked of which goods. Design Release 2.1's germinal journey moves goods through Great Britain under Transit, and the copy rule carries the live-animals arrival and transit countries pages across, so the germinal products set asks for transit countries on the same terms as live animals, whenever the means of transport is rail or road (req-2166). Nothing is set aside here: the data page's silence on the set's other live-animal fields still stands as recorded, and the condition bullet that reads transited countries as applying to the animals journey only sits in the page's arrival half, which the arrival area weighs.

conflicts.about: Whether the same-checks rule reaches the germinal products set's contact address page, which the 26 October ruling does not name.

positions.says: The ruling names only live animals and high-risk plants and says nothing about the germinal-products set or any other frontend with both save buttons.
No page is an exception to the same-checks rule.
The germinal set is copied from the live-animals feature folders once their twins are built.

conflicts.outcome: The 26 October ruling ranks above the 9 October ruling and says no page is an exception, so the rule reaches the germinal set too; the 9 October ruling makes the germinal set a copy of the live-animals feature folders, so its contact address page carries the live-animals page's behaviour without needing a rule of its own. The ruling's silence on the germinal set is a gap in its wording, not a carve-out, and the 27 November ruling names the germinal copy outright. The set-wide settlement, covering the germinal set's own pages as well as its copies, is c-339.

conflicts.about: Whether the germinal set's commodity search is built in this programme or belongs to the separate commodity-search ticket.

positions.says: The germinal set's copy of the search-as-you-type work follows the live-animals one into the waiting-on-design theme, and V4's germinal catalogue in that increment is blocked on MDM.
Design question 3, commodity search as you type, moves to waiting-on-design with the germinal set's copy following the live-animals increment.
The commodity search is handled by a different ticket, not by this work.
A search listing germinal codes belongs to the separate commodity-search ticket, not to this backlog.

conflicts.outcome: Sam's 10 November ruling ranks above the 9 October afternoon ruling and takes the commodity search, the germinal search included, out of this backlog and into the separate commodity-search ticket, whose design call waits on that ticket being implemented. So the germinal set's search results, their ordering and their live-region announcement are out of scope here (req-1782), and the germinal commodity page goes ahead with the server-side search behind the Search button that the live page already has (req-1927). The afternoon ruling's design-question-3 claim is not overruled: it still records what the live-animals half of that work was placed in, which the commodities area weighs.
